Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:45: And likewise among the things that cause cleaving is for a person to seclude himself part of the day when he contemplates the greatness of the Creator of all, as explained in the Gate of Fear and the Gate of Love, and recite with his mouth the latter speeches of Job, saying them with understanding, calmly, and in a loud voice; and likewise several verses from the psalms of King David, peace be upon him, that recount the wonders of the LORD and His greatness. And so Rabbenu Tam wrote in Sefer HaYashar, that a person should accustom himself to read once a week the response beginning "then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind" (Job 38:3), "gird up your loins now like a man." And Rabbenu Yonah wrote that one should read every day the passage (Deuteronomy 10:12), "what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear," and so it is good to read both this and that.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:46: And likewise, when a person reads Pesukei D'Zimra every day and recites them with intention and in a loud voice, he draws cleaving upon himself; and so let him be constant every day in reading the Book of Psalms with intention and in a loud voice in the synagogue - and how good it is if he also intends, in the secret way, some of the appellations customary in the Zohar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:47: And behold, just as song causes cleaving, so too Torah is called song and causes cleaving, as they explained, of blessed memory, on "and in the night His song is with me" (Psalms 42:9) - the joyous song of Torah is only at night. And behold, the whole reality of song, whether the joyous song of Torah or the other songs, is all to give arousal to the Shechinah, as they say (ibid. 30:13), "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent; O LORD my God, I will give thanks to You forever" - and it cannot be explained that David meant "forever" only through psalms, for when would his Torah study be done? Rather certainly the occupation with Torah too is part of the thanksgiving and praise, as he said (ibid. 119:7), "I will thank You with uprightness of heart, when I learn Your righteous judgments."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:48: And part of the love of the King is to honor Him and sing before Him in the synagogue, just as it is customary to sing before a king of flesh and blood - and the praise of a king is his glory, along the lines of (Psalms 29:9), "and in His temple all say, Glory," and it says, "ascribe to the LORD glory and strength, ascribe to the LORD the glory of His name" - and in what is His name glorified? Certainly through praise, song, and lauding.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:49: And in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, page 73a), Rabbi Elazar opened and said (Isaiah 25:1), "O LORD, You are my God; I will exalt You, I will praise Your name, for You have done wonderful things, counsels of old, faithfulness and truth" - how much people should gaze upon the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, and praise His glory - for whoever knows how to praise his Master properly, the Holy One, blessed be He, performs his will, and moreover, blessings increase above and below; and therefore, whoever knows how to praise his Master and unify His Name is beloved above and desired below, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is praised through him in His glory, and of him it is written (Isaiah 49:3), "and He said to me, You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified" - to this point. And further, in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 250a) on the verse (Isaiah 10:30), "cry aloud with your voice," and so on, they said, in these words: and therefore, whoever increases praises to the Holy One, blessed be He, increases peace above - therefore, "hearken, Laish" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:50: And because we do not know how to arrange praises, it is good that we say the praises of King David, peace be upon him. King David, peace be upon him, requested that his psalms be recited in synagogues and study halls, as it is said (Psalms 61:5), "I will dwell in Your tent forever [olamim]" - David said, Master of the universe, may it be Your will that a word from my mouth be said in this world (Bechorot 31b). And further they said in the Midrash (cf. Midrash Tehillim, Psalm 1): Rabbi Yirmiyah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, it is written, "I will dwell in Your tent forever" - and does it enter your mind that David sought to dwell in two worlds? Rather, he said, may it be Your will that they read and mention me in synagogues and study halls as though I were alive - to this point. And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (ibid.) that David asked that they study and read them and receive reward for them as for [studying the laws of] leprosy and tents, as it is said (ibid. 19:15), "let the words of my mouth be acceptable."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:51: And in any case, one who reads the Book of Psalms in the synagogue, or liturgical poems and the like, should not raise his voice if he does not have a pleasant voice - and so they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 249b) on the verse (Isaiah 10:30), "cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim; hearken, Laish," in these words: "cry aloud with your voice" - this verse is said of the Community of Israel, because she praises the Holy One, blessed be He, with a praising voice, and therefore "cry aloud with your voice." From here we learn that whoever wishes to praise the Holy One, blessed be He, with his voice needs a pleasant voice that will blend with the others who hear him, and if not, he should not rise to raise his voice. Come and see, the Levites who come from this side, as it is written (Numbers 8:25), "and from the age of fifty years he shall return from the service of the work," and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:52: And just as the songs of Torah cause cleaving to the LORD, blessed be He, so the songs that women sing, which are words of lust and foul speech, cause the soul to be separated from the bond of life, and at the very least are idle words that have no substance in them. And how many people of base soul are drawn after these base songs and destroy their souls! Of them the prophet said (Amos 5:23), "take away from Me the noise of your songs, and I will not hear the melody of your lyres," and he further said (ibid. 6:5), "who pluck on the strings of the lyre like David, they devise for themselves instruments of song."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:53: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 31a): Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rashbi, it is forbidden for a person to fill his mouth with laughter in this world, as it is said (Psalms 126:2), "then will our mouth be filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing; then will they say among the nations, the LORD has done great things for these" - it was said of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish that he did not fill his mouth with laughter in this world from when he finished learning this teaching from the mouth of Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:54: And Rabbi Yitzchak Alfasi, peace be upon him, copied, alongside this saying from Berachot, everything relevant found in the Gemara, and therefore we saw fit to copy his words, in these words: we learn in Gittin, first chapter: they sent to Mar Ukva, "from where do we know that music is forbidden?" He sketched and wrote to them (Hosea 9:1), "do not rejoice, O Israel, to exultation, like the peoples," and should he not have sent us (Isaiah 24:9), "they shall not drink wine with song," and so on? Had it been derived from that verse alone, I would have said this refers only to song accompanied by a vessel [instrument], but song by mouth is permitted - this teaches us that it too is forbidden. Ravina found Mar bar Rav Ashi weaving a wreath for his daughter, and said to him, do you not hold as it is said (Ezekiel 21:31), "remove the mitre, and take off the crown" - when the mitre is on the High Priest's head, let the crown be on every man's head; when the mitre is removed from the High Priest's head, the crown is removed from every man's head? He said to him, this applies only to men, in the likeness of the High Priest, but not to women.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:55: And we learn at the end of Sotah: Rav said, an ear that hears song should be uprooted. Rava said, song in a house is destruction at the threshold, as it is said (Zephaniah 2:14), "a voice shall sing in the window; devastation shall be at the threshold." Rav Yosef said, when men sing and women respond, it is licentiousness; when women sing and men respond, it is like fire in flax. What is the practical difference? To determine which is worse than the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:56: Rabbi Yochanan said: whoever drinks wine to the accompaniment of four kinds of music brings five punishments upon the world, as it is said (Isaiah 5:11), "woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink, who linger late into the night till wine inflames them; and the harp, and the lyre, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts" - what is written after it (ibid. 5:13)? "Therefore My people are gone into exile for lack of knowledge, and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:57: The Gaon explained: what they said, "song by mouth is forbidden," refers to melodies of a person's love for his fellow, and praising the beauty of a beautiful woman, such as what the Ishmaelites call "ash'ar" [poetry] - but words of songs and praises and remembrance of the kindnesses of the Holy One, blessed be He, no person of Israel refrains from these, and it is the custom of all Israel to say them at wedding houses and feast houses in a voice of melody and a voice of joy, and we have not seen anyone protest this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:58: We learn in chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 101a): our Rabbis taught, one who reads a verse from the Song of Songs and turns it into a kind of song, and one who reads a verse out of its [proper] time, brings evil to the world - because the Torah girds itself with sackcloth and stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, and says, Master of the universe, Your children have made me like a lyre that scoffers play upon. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: My daughter, if so, what shall My children do when they eat and drink and rejoice? She said before Him, Master of the universe, if they are masters of Scripture, let them occupy themselves with Scripture, with the Prophets and the Writings; and if they are masters of Mishnah, let them occupy themselves with Mishnah, with halachot and aggadot; and if they are masters of Talmud, let them occupy themselves with Talmud - with the laws of Passover on Passover, the laws of Shavuot on Shavuot, the laws of the festival on the festival. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar testified in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya: one who reads a verse in its [proper] time brings good to the world, as it is said (Proverbs 15:23), "and a word spoken in its proper time, how good it is" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:59: And in the Tosefta to Sanhedrin, chapter 12, we say: Rabbi Akiva says, one who trills his voice over the Song of Songs at a banquet house and turns it into a kind of song has no share in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:60: And behold, it is already known what the pious one said in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3), that this world and the World to Come are like two rival wives - when you please one, you anger the other. And as pertains to our subject, know that it is impossible for a person to be cleaved to the joy of his Owner as long as he is joyful in worldly pleasure and in eating and drinking, as the prophet said (Isaiah 22:13), "and behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" - what is written after it? "And it was revealed in my ears by the LORD of hosts, surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till you die," and so on. And King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:4), "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth." And the prophet Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I sat not in the assembly of merrymakers, nor rejoiced." And our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Pesikta (D'Rav Kahana, pesikta 15): the Community of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I did not enter the theaters and circuses of the gentiles and sport with them; because of Your hand I sat alone - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:61: And therefore it is not fitting to rejoice in the joy of this world, for it all passes away - as our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded in Vayikra Rabbah, at the beginning of Parashat Acharei Mot, in these words, on the verse (Psalms 75:5), "I said to the boastful, do not boast; and to the wicked, do not lift up the horn" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the wicked: the righteous did not rejoice in My world, and you seek to rejoice? Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: the heel of Adam the first man outshone the orb of the sun - how much more so his facial countenance! And do not wonder, for it is the way of the world that a person makes a garment - one for himself and one for his house - for whom does he make the finer one? Not for himself. So Adam the first man was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the orb of the sun for the service of [His] creatures. Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Chama bar Chanina: the Holy One, blessed be He, tied thirteen bridal canopies for him in the Garden of Eden, as it is said (Ezekiel 28:13), "you were in Eden, the garden of God," and so on - and after all this praise: "for dust you are, and to dust you shall return."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:62: Abraham did not rejoice in the world, and you seek to rejoice? A son was born to him at a hundred years, and in the end the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "take now your son," and he walked a journey of three days, and so on. Israel did not rejoice in My world - it does not say, "Israel rejoiced in his Maker," but "shall rejoice" [yismach, future tense] - they are destined to rejoice in the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the time to come. As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not rejoice in His world, as it is said, "the LORD shall rejoice in His works" - it does not say "rejoiced," but "shall rejoice" - the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to rejoice in the deeds of the righteous in the time to come - to this point, relevant here. We have skipped much of the discourse not needed for our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:63: And it is written in the book of Middot found among us in manuscript (Orchot Tzaddikim, Gate of Joy), that one should not increase laughter, because it diminishes fear [of Heaven], in these words: at the time of laughter one cannot direct any fear of the Name, his God; and all the more so if he laughs in outings or in gambling, in which the fear of God is not upon him. Therefore a person should chastise his son that he not increase laughter, and not acquire for him a teacher or friend to laugh with, as it is said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I sat not in the assembly of merrymakers," and it is written (Proverbs 14:23), "in all labor there is profit." And there is much evil in joy and laughter, such as rejoicing at the misfortune of one's fellow when some evil mishap of this world befalls him - concerning this it is said (ibid. 24:17), "do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbles."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:64: And there is another joy worse than this - such as rejoicing when one's fellows stumble in the service of the Creator, blessed be He, or rejoicing at their lack of knowledge. Every servant who serves his master faithfully must know what to say before his master, and you should be pained when you see people rebelling against their Master, and mourn over them - then he is a faithful servant. But if the servant sees people belittling and reviling his master and he rejoices, this is not a faithful servant. And behold, Scripture says (Psalms 147:11), "the LORD favors those who fear Him" - and whoever rejoices at his fellow's stumbling, his will is not according to the will of the Creator. Concerning this Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah prayed (Berachot 28b): "may my colleagues not stumble in a matter of halachah so that I rejoice over them, and may I not stumble so that they rejoice over me" - and Rabbi Nechunya prayed about this because he saw that it was a common thing for one to rejoice at his fellow's mishap so that he would be victorious over his fellow and gain a reputation - and he even saw that important people were not careful about this. Therefore, every person whose will is like the will of God should be pained that God's will was not done, and a person should pray even for his enemy, that he serve the Creator - and he should direct his heart in prayer, in the blessing "You favor," and in the blessing "return us, our Father," and "forgive us, our Father," for all of Israel, those who love him and those who hate him - and so in all the blessings, for how can it be that a doctor prays for the sickness of his people Israel while he does not want his fellow to be healed? And so for the other blessings. And because this evil inclination is common in the hearts of every person and he does not notice this matter, it was therefore written to warn the fear of the LORD, blessed be He, to prepare their hearts to God with complete and true intention, to pour out their souls before the Name for all of Israel, those who love him and those who hate him - and thus "you shall love your neighbor as yourself" is fulfilled, and "he who has clean hands shall grow stronger."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:65: And there is another joy and laughter worse than this - such as one who laughs at one who is careful in the service of the Creator, blessed be He, and who fulfills His commandments. And there are four evils in this: the first, that he darkens his own soul from the light of the commandments - when he despises and laughs at those who fulfill the commandments, the commandments become despicable in his eyes. The second, that perhaps because of the laughter the righteous one will refrain from his righteousness, for he cannot bear the laughter. The third, that many people who have not been tested to walk in the ways of the Name will be unable to repent because of the laughter, and will walk in darkness all their days - it follows that this scoffer not only prevents his fellow from the abundant good hidden away for the righteous, but brings him down to the depths of Sheol; and behold, this scoffer is included in the punishment of one who causes the many to sin. The fourth, that he is like robbers who stand at the crossroads and cut off the feet of those bringing gifts to the king - are they not enemies of the king, and their evil very great?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:66: And there is another joy bitter as wormwood - such as those who pursue adultery, theft, and other transgressions, and rejoice when they attain their evil desires. Concerning this it is said (Proverbs 2:14), "who rejoice to do evil, who delight in the perversities of evil" - and their punishment is great, down to the depths of Sheol.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:67: And there is yet another joy, mixed with the smoke that rises against all the commandments, which causes the fear of the Name, blessed be He, to be forgotten from people's hearts - such as those who get drunk and rejoice in feast houses, and the end of that joy is grief, for many corruptions come from the way of the laughter of feasting. And who is as wise as Solomon son of David, who said (ibid. 23:29), "who has woe? who has sorrow? who has contentions? who has complaining? who has wounds without cause? who has redness of eyes? those who linger long over wine, those who go to seek out mixed wine." Also the prophet Isaiah said (Isaiah 5:12), "but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of His hands," and it is written (Proverbs 20:1), "wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler, and whoever is deceived by it is not wise."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:68: And after we have explained the nature of joy and its opposite, we saw fit to explain in several ways in which we are obligated in it, and we say: since it is true that love and joy are both one matter, as explained, whoever wishes to be pious [chassid] and to be called a lover from the seed of Abraham, of whom it is said (Isaiah 41:8), "the seed of Abraham My lover," must be joyful when blessing the Holy One, blessed be He, with the blessings over enjoyment, and likewise in his prayer, his Torah, and his commandments, and in receiving people with joy, and on the days of the festivals, as we explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:69: In his blessings he should intend to give praise and thanksgiving to the Cause of all who created that thing, and through the praise he cleaves to the love of the Creator and His greatness and exaltedness. We have already said that all the supernal beings and the souls above all praise the Creator because of the good they received from Him, and forever the Cause of all - His flow and His light are never withheld from flowing forth. And for this we are obligated to bless Him, and for this reason is the matter of the blessings the men of the Great Assembly instituted over every single thing - so that we remember the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His greatness and exaltedness, and His constant providence with us at every time, that He created that thing through His flow, by the power of His supernal attributes, so that the lower ones benefit from His flow, and through it we are cleaved to Him forever. Therefore one must give praise and blessing to the Creator with a good heart and a good eye and with joy - and so they explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Bamidbar), where he said on the verse (Psalms 115:12), "the LORD has remembered us, He will bless" - that when a person mentions his fellow's praise, he must bless him so that the evil eye not rule over him; and he said, whoever blesses his fellow requires that the Holy One, blessed be He, bless him with a good eye and a good heart - one who blesses the Holy One, blessed be He, all the more so requires a good eye and a good heart and love of heart; therefore, "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:70: And behold, from matters of this world a person may take an example for love of the Holy One, blessed be He - it is known that one who gives a gift to his fellow without any prior favor from his fellow, the recipient of that gift is obligated to love the giver, even if the gift is small. And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, who gives everything and gives to all, as he says (1 Chronicles 29:14), "for everything comes from You" - without doubt a person is obligated in love toward Him, blessed be He. And when a person contemplates this while blessing the blessing over enjoyment, love is aroused in his heart. However, one who blesses without intending to give praise to the Creator, blessed be He, is punished, as they said in Sefer Chassidim - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:71: And further, one who blesses with joy and a good heart becomes a chariot for the attribute of Chesed - for just as the attribute of Chesed flows with generosity, without severity, and with will and joy, since joy is from its side, as explained, so too the one blessing; and this is along the lines of (Genesis 12:3), "and I will bless those who bless you" - for just as he desires to flow blessings to the Community of Israel from the side of Chesed, so they flow to him from Chesed - and this is called "a good eye."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:72: And just as a person is obligated to be joyful on days of joy, so must he mourn on days of distress, along the lines of the four fasts, "the fast of the fourth [month]," and so on (Zechariah 8:19), and the twenty-one days between the seventeenth of Tammuz and the ninth of Av, which are all days of pain and sorrow. And so on days that are not days of joy, it is good that he mourn every day over the destruction of the Temple and over His Name profaned among the nations, as it is said in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, copied in the Yalkut (Parashat Ki Tisa, section 391), that one must sigh over the honor of the Omnipresent and the honor of Israel all his days, and yearn, desire, and anticipate the glory of Jerusalem, the glory of Israel, the glory of the Temple, and the salvation soon to sprout forth - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:73: And in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, end of page 17), they explained, of blessed memory: Rabbi Yehuda came to Rabbi Elazar, and found him sitting with his hand on his mouth, sad. He said to him, what is my master occupied with? He said to him, it is written (Proverbs 16:15), "in the light of the king's countenance is life." And from this we shall understand the obligation of humility and sadness - for if you raise your eyes to the heavens you will see the diminishment of the flow, for all faces have gathered gloom (variant: paleness) from the miracles and wonders of days of old and ancient years - and therefore it is fitting to banish natural joy and to direct our spirits toward Him, to make this a foundation, that it is the satisfaction of the Omnipresent upon us, that He flow into our souls in His goodness upon us, in the secret of creation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:74: He further said in Pesikta Rabbati (chapter 26): "she who bore seven languishes" (Jeremiah 15:9) - Jeremiah said, when I was going up to Jerusalem, I lifted my eyes and saw a certain woman sitting on top of the mountain, clothed in black, her hair disheveled, crying out and seeking who would comfort her, and I was crying out and seeking who would comfort me. I drew near to her and spoke with her: if you are a woman, speak with me; and if you are a spirit, depart from before me. She answered and said to me, do you not recognize me? I am she who had seven sons; their father went overseas, until, while I was still going up and weeping over him, a second messenger came and told me that the house had fallen upon your seven sons and killed them, and I do not know for whom to weep or for whom to tear my hair. I said to her, who are you, better than Mother Zion who has become a pasture for the beasts of the field? She answered and said to me, I am your mother Zion, who has become a pasture for the beasts of the field; I am the mother of the seven, as it is written, "she who bore seven languishes." Jeremiah said to her, your wound is like the wound of an enemy: "shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit, O Jerusalem" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:75: And in Midrash Eichah, from the Zohar, they elaborated at length on the matter of weeping over the exile and the destruction - see there. And whoever mourns over Jerusalem merits to see her comfort, as it is said (Isaiah 66:10), "rejoice with her in joy, all you who mourn over her" (Ta'anit 30b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:1: After we have explained, in the previous chapters, the nature of love and the things that give birth to love, as found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, we wish to explain the preparations a person must undertake with his body to acquire love, so that it be fixed in the heart like a peg that will not slip.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:2: And these preparations Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, peace be upon him, explained (Avodah Zarah 20b), in these words: our Rabbis taught, "and you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10) - that a person should not have improper thoughts by day and come to impurity at night. From here Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said: Torah brings one to watchfulness [zehirut], watchfulness brings one to alacrity [zerizut], alacrity brings one to cleanliness [nekiyut], cleanliness brings one to separation [perishut], separation brings one to purity [taharah], purity brings one to holiness [kedushah], holiness brings one to humility [anavah], humility brings one to fear of sin [yirat chet], fear of sin brings one to piety [chassidut], piety brings one to the holy spirit [ru'ach ha-kodesh], the holy spirit brings one to the resurrection of the dead - and piety is greater than all of them, as it is said (Psalms 89:20), "then You spoke in a vision to Your pious ones." And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disputes this, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, humility is greater than all of them, as it is said (Isaiah 61:1), "the spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good tidings to the humble" - it does not say "to the pious," but "to the humble" - from this you learn that humility is greater than all of them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:3: And behold, according to Rabbi Pinchas's view, that piety is greater than all of them, this is why we intended to explain this discourse for the purposes of the study of love. And the reason is that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar that piety and love are both one matter, and Rabbi Pinchas, peace be upon him, was crowned with them - and the proof of this is what he said in the Zohar Bereshit (end of page 11), in the second commandment, which is love: Rabbi Elazar said, father, beloved one, I have heard of it. He said to him, say it, my son, before Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, for he stands at this rank. And in Parashat Acharei Mot (page 62), Rabbi Shimon, peace be upon him, praised Rabbi Pinchas for the attribute of piety, and expounded to praise him the verse (Psalms 149:5), "let the pious exult in glory," in these words: behold, Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair is the crown of Chesed, the supernal head; therefore the pious inherit the glory that is above - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:4: And the matter is simple, that love and kindness are all one, as it is said (Jeremiah 31:2), "I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore with kindness have I drawn you," and similarly (Psalms 31:24), "love the LORD, all His pious ones." And therefore we saw fit to explain this discourse, which explains the levels that lead to piety, which is love - and when a person fulfills these levels, love, which is piety, will be fixed in his heart, and he will be cleaved to his God always, in such a manner that he will merit the holy spirit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:5: Rashi, peace be upon him, explained this beraita, in these words: "and you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (Deuteronomy 23:10), and next to it, "if there be among you a man who is not clean because of an accident by night" - warning him to be careful not to come to such a thing. "Torah" - through his engagement with it, and also because he sees and understands the warnings within it, and is thereby guarded. "Alacrity" - one who is guarded beforehand so that transgression not come into his hand, for since he does not have improper thoughts, he does not come to impurity. "Watchfulness" - when a transgression comes into his hand, he is careful to guard himself from stumbling in it - and thus we say in [the chapter] "Kol HaBasar" (Chullin 107b): does this not mean, "one who is watchful and does not touch it"? No - rather one who is alert and washes his hands beforehand. "Cleanliness" - clean of sin. "Separation" - he separates himself even from what is permitted, to be stringent with himself. "Purity" - bright and refined, superior to cleanliness. "To the holy spirit" - to have the Shechinah rest upon him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:6: And Rabbenu Nissim copied Rashi's words, peace be upon him, and added an explanation of humility, fear of sin, and piety, in these words: from this he comes to humility, because he despises the affairs of this world; and from it he comes to fear of sin, for he fears it as one fears an enemy; and from this he comes to piety - that all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:7: And now we wish to broaden the explanation of the words of Rashi, of blessed memory, peace be upon him, and to explain each and every word mentioned in this discourse, according to how it is used in Torah, Prophets, and Writings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:8: "Torah brings one to alacrity" - this matter is explained in several places, that Talmud brings one to deed, and they said in Torat Kohanim (beginning of Parashat Bechukotai): "if you walk in My statutes" - that you labor in Torah; "you shall keep and do them" - one who learns in order to do; "if you will not hearken and will not do" - whoever does not learn does not do; in the end he despises others, in the end he despises the Sages, in the end he does not allow others to act, in the end he does not acknowledge the commandments given to Moses at Sinai, in the end he denies the fundamental principle - to this point. Behold, it is explained that one who is occupied with Torah is necessarily brought thereby to the deed, as Rashi, of blessed memory, explained, that because he sees the warnings and punishments written in it, he is guarded from sin.
